analyst_view.overall: Early view: Marseille are 31st with 3 points and need a home win, but they are in better shape than that suggests: they won 1-0 at Leverkusen through a late Amine Gouiri goal and then 2-1 at Lens in Ligue 1. Levski Sofia (10th, 7 points) have been hard to beat, with only seven goals in their four league-phase games combined.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean lower: Marseille have scored only twice in four European games and won their last two matches by a single goal, and Levski's games have finished 0-1, 1-1, 2-1 and 1-0. A Marseille win looks likely, but 2-0 or 2-1 fits better than a high score.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 7.1 of them for Marseille. That fits a game in which Levski, who have built their points on defence, spend long spells in their own half at the Velodrome, so I stay close to 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Levski's games have been tight and controlled rather than bad-tempered, and Marseille should have the ball, so I stay with the number; a packed Velodrome and a narrow score could add a late booking.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, which is a lot. Marseille's European attack has been blunt (two goals in four games) and they won at Leverkusen with only eight shots, while Levski's games have been short on chances, so I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. For the same reasons I lean lower: Marseille had only two shots on target at Leverkusen, and Levski's low-scoring games point to 8 or 9 in total, most of them from Marseille.
